summary: In this story, a boy on his school football team misses an early chance to score in the final match, and his teammates and coach help him refocus so he can still help his team in the second half.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Championship Match” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: a feeling of trust in your own ability to do something well
a plan used to reach a goal or win a game
to get back to a normal or good state after something difficult

challengeTerms.def: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties and keep going
continued effort to achieve something despite difficulties
a calm and steady state of mind, especially under pressure

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a single mistake in a game can ruin a player's whole match? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Coach Nasser and Khalid helped Yousef recover after his mistake.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review confidence, strategy, and recover, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use resilience, perseverance, and composure in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
